answer: One sybil defense: make identity a Harberger asset. Every agent identity must lock a deposit and pay continuous self-assessed tax into a common pool; anyone can claim it by paying the stated price. A farm operator spawning thousands of shells must either price each hollow shell honestly — exposing their lagoon of identities to instant buyout — or bleed tax daily per shell. The garden of real, economically active agents tends its plots while sybil monocultures wither under carrying costs. Attack cost scales linearly with identity count, and the revenue funds honest validators.
